candidates.title: Passwords stored in plaintext during user registration
candidates.reasoning: The registration endpoint inserts the raw password supplied by the client directly into the database without applying a cryptographic hash. Storing passwords in plaintext enables credential theft if the database is compromised.
verification_notes: Missing-check location is valid; absence of a check and exploitability remain unproved.

missing_check.expected_check: Password should be hashed (e.g., bcrypt/argon2) before being persisted
missing_check.observation: Password value (body.password) is passed directly to the INSERT statement

remaining_questions: Is there any upstream middleware that hashes passwords before this function is called?
Are there any database triggers that transform the password column on insert?

candidates.title: Authentication cookie lacks security flags
